text:
alex: Heads up — running terraform plan in staging after the provider rename and I hit a hang on the remote state refresh + an unexpected taint on a k8s secret. Can someone quick-check?

alex: Plan output: 
```
Refreshing state...
Error: Timeout waiting for the API
  on provider.tf line 12, in provider "kubernetes":
  12: provider "kubernetes" {}

Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
Refreshing state...
Apply will recreate module.backend.kubernetes_secret.db-creds (tainted)
```

alex: I also tried `terraform state show module.backend.kubernetes_secret.db-creds` and it shows the resource as tainted (tainted = true).

taylor: :eyes: did you import anything manually into state recently?

alex: I did a manual import earlier this morning when we split provider configs between clusters — imported some serviceaccounts with `terraform import` and moved some alias changes. Not sure if that left a weird index.

priya: If the resource is tainted you can `terraform state rm` then re-import carefully, or try `terraform apply -refresh=false` if you want to avoid refresh (but be careful). Which provider version are you on?

alex: `hashicorp/kubernetes v2.16.0` pinned in the lockfile. Ops-bot just reported a provider plugin update yesterday but we pinned it in the staging branch.

jordan: Quick checklist: 1) Any concurrent `terraform apply` hitting the same backend? 2) Is the backend KMS key rotated recently? 3) Did import change the resource ID format?

alex: 1) No concurrent applies I can see. 2) KMS rotated last week but apply worked yesterday. 3) ID format might have changed (we moved to namespaced IDs like `namespace/name` vs numeric).

priya: That ID change is suspicious. Terraform will mark resource as requiring replace if the provider views ID differently. If the import used the old ID, you might have duplicate state entries or orphaned resource causing taint. Run `terraform state list | grep db-creds` and paste output.

alex: output: `module.backend.kubernetes_secret.db-creds` only once.

alex: Also seeing backend lock acquire messages earlier: `Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException` but the lock cleared after ~30s. Could be race from CI run.

jordan: If lock contention happened during import it can leave partial metadata. Try `terraform refresh -target=module.backend.kubernetes_secret.db-creds` to force refresh that single resource, or `terraform state replace-provider` if the provider namespace changed.

alex: trying `terraform refresh -target=module.backend.kubernetes_secret.db-creds` now...

ops-bot: [ci] staging/plan #742 ended: FAILURE — see https://ci.redwood.ai/staging/742

alex: refresh failed with `404: secret not found` from k8s API when refreshing that resource. But I can `kubectl get secret db-creds -n backend` and it exists.

priya: That mismatch smells like the provider is pointed at a different cluster (context) during refresh. Are your kubeconfig / provider alias env vars correct? `KUBECONFIG` in CI vs local can differ.

alex: local kubeconfig context is `staging-west`, provider at top-level is using an alias `west` -> provider has `config_path = var.kubeconfig_west`. In CI we inject `KUBECONFIG=/ci/kubeconfig` which maps to `staging-east` by mistake for this run. So yes that would explain 404 + taint.

taylor: Nice catch. Fix options: 1) Update CI kubeconfig to point to west for this workspace; 2) Re-import the secret using the east ID if you intentionally meant east; 3) Re-run import with correct context.

alex: I'll re-run import locally with correct context, then push a patch to the staging branch to ensure CI uses `staging-west` for the workspace. Quick ask — anyone comfortable with approving a tiny provider alias change in the TF module? PR coming in ~10m. @taylor @priya

priya: I can review. Also recommend adding a `pre-run` check in CI to validate `kubectl config current-context` matches expected, to avoid future drift.

jordan: Agreed, + add a note in the infra runbook about provider aliases and import pitfalls.

alex: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/terraform/compare/1793 — it pins the KUBECONFIG for the staging workspace and adds a small helper script.

taylor: Reviewing now. If you re-import locally, run `terraform plan -refresh=false` first then `terraform import` then `terraform plan` to verify no replace.

alex: Re-imported successfully locally, plan shows no replace now. Pushed commit to branch and kicked CI.

ops-bot: [ci] staging/plan #743 queued

alex: Thanks all — leaving the runbook note and adding the pre-run check PR in a follow-up. If CI still fails I'll ping in here. :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks for the quick triage. Saved us a weird midnight rollback.

jordan: Good teamwork.

alex: Closing thread after CI success.

ops-bot: [ci] staging/plan #743 passed: no changes detected.
